sources.citation: Murray, Jean Christine. 2018. Ninde: A Grammar Sketch and Topics in Nominal Morphology. MA thesis, University of Waikato. xv+225 pp. hdl 10289/12126
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1.6 Phonology (pp.15-28) covers consonant inventory, vowel inventory, phonotactics (syllable structure) and orthography; the words stress/accent/prosody do not occur (a full-text search for stress/accent count 0); only rising intonation in yes/no questions is noted.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Kevin J. 2023. Ninde as a Mixed Language: A Reconstruction of Proto North Central Malekula and Proto South West Bay. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. https://escholarship.org/uc/item/15r1q351
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No synchronic stress rule. Diachronic phonology of Ninde (sec. 5.3). p.311: 'Reconstructions from Ninde will likely fail to predict forms like these in Avava and Neverver, and it may have something to do with underdescribed stress placement.' p.341: 'With no representation of stress, any sound changes that interacted with stress are missing.' pp.228-229 discuss Charpentier's post-tonic 'destressed' vowels, but for Lendamboi, not Ninde.

sources.citation: Crouch, Caroline. 2018-. Ninde documentation and orthographic design project. ELAR deposit (ELDP SG0424), SOAS London; plus Crouch's and Schaefer's talks on Ninde at APLL9 (Paris, June 2017).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Trained phonetician's documentation corpus; written documents in the deposit (orthography proposal, notes) or the APLL9 abstract may contain a prosody/stress statement; also the raw material for an instrumental check.

sources.citation: Murray, Jean. 2016. Exploring the Phonological System of Ninde (Malekula, Vanuatu). Te Kete Aronui vol. 7, University of Waikato. 22 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Segmental inventory, allophony and orthography proposal only; no mention of stress, accent or prosody (a full-text search for stress/accent count 0). downloaded from Internet Archive copy of the Waikato URL cited by Murray 2018.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2014. Unexpected final vowel retention in Malakula. Open Linguistics 1: 1-16. doi:10.2478/opli-2014-0001
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 'Ninde' treats historical loss/retention of POc final vowels (conditioned by final-vowel height); the words stress/accent/tonic do not occur anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: A comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603. Canberra: ANU. Section 3.11 Ninde, pp.39-41.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 C59 2009
sources.note: No stress placement for Ninde. p.39: 'There is no published modern phonemic analysis of Ninde.' p.40: the extra vowels o-umlaut, u-umlaut, schwa 'may be no more than unstressed variants of the five undoubted phonemic vowels'. Other language sections in the book carry an explicit 'Stress is penultimate' line; the Ninde section does not. Sec. 2.1.3 (p.16): PNCV word stress 'most likely on the penultimate vowel'.

sources.note: Largest first-hand phonetic record of Ninde (atlas point 6); p.63 has phonetic notes and Charpentier marked tonic/post-tonic vowels for neighbouring varieties, so his Ninde transcriptions or notes may indicate stress position.

sources.note: Archive deposit (audio/video/ELAN, written documents); ELAR search page seen, no analytic document on Ninde prosody identified. Crossref shows Crouch's published phonetics papers are on Georgian; no Ninde publication found. Schaefer 2023 fn.27 cites her (p.c.) only on prenasalised stops.
